latin_text: Οἷά τις πτηνὸς αἰθέριος ὁ Παῦλος διέθει, κύκλῳ διατρέχων τὴν οἰκουμένην. Nicephor. Callist. ecclesiast. histor. lib. 3. cap. 1. καθάπερ ὑποπτερός τις πᾶσαν διαδραμὼν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐσαγήνευσε. Menæa Græc. Jun. 29.

translation_history.english: "Like a winged ethereal being, Paul ran about, traversing the inhabited world in a circuit." Nicephorus Callistus, Ecclesiastical History, book 3, chapter 1. "As if winged, having traversed the whole inhabited world, he caught it in his net." Greek Menaia, June 29.
translation_history.notes: ἐσαγήνευσε literally 'caught with a dragnet,' a Patristic image for evangelistic gathering.

latin_text: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς. Niceph. hist. eccles. lib. 12. cap. 34. Vix triginta annorum spatio et Romanos, et Persas, et Parthos, et Medos, et Indos, et Scythas, et Sauromatas, et Sarracenos, et omne prorsus humanum genus sub jugum mitteret veritatis, &c. Chrysost. homil. 4. de laudib. Pauli. Clemens in epistola ad Corinthios pag. 8. de eodem: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. In oriente ac occidente verbi præco factus, illustrem fidei suæ fainam sortitus est, in justitia mundum universum instruens, et ad occidentis terminos veniens, et sub imperatoribus martyrium subiens, sic e mundo migravit.

translation_history.english: "Having gone through nearly the whole earth, and having contended in the gospel for Christ for thirty-five years." Nicephorus, Ecclesiastical History, book 12, chapter 34. "Within the space of scarcely thirty years he brought the Romans, the Persians, the Parthians, the Medes, the Indians, the Scythians, the Sauromatae, the Saracens, and absolutely the entire human race under the yoke of truth, etc." Chrysostom, Homily 4 on the Praises of Paul. Clement, in his Epistle to the Corinthians, page 8, concerning the same: "Having become a herald in the East and in the West, he received the noble renown of his faith, having taught righteousness to the whole world, and having come to the limit of the West, and having borne witness before the rulers, he thus departed from the world." "Having become a preacher of the word in the East and in the West, he obtained the illustrious fame of his faith, instructing the whole world in righteousness, and coming to the boundaries of the West, and undergoing martyrdom under the emperors, he thus departed from the world."
translation_history.notes: Final sentence is the Latin rendering of the preceding Greek from Clement; both are translated for completeness.
